steps-over-integers.label: steps over integers (state transitions with integer and Boolean values)
steps-over-integers.legend_header: Theory: steps over integers (state transitions with integer and Boolean values). x′ is x after the step; ¬ is negation. The prime is not negation or a derivative; Boolean algebra uses x′ for "not x".

forall: the statement after the colon holds for each {v} in {domain}; true if {domain} is empty
exists: the statement after the colon holds for some {v} in {domain}; false if {domain} is empty
exists1: one and no more member satisfies the statement; false if the domain is empty
=>: when the left side is true the right side must be; when it is false there is no demand
<=>: both sides have the same truth value
not: true exactly when the following statement is false
or: at least one statement must hold; both may hold
ceil: the least integer at or above u/v; v must be positive
floor: the greatest integer at or below u/v; v must be positive
count: the number of distinct members that satisfy the condition
group: explicit grouping; the enclosed expression is one operand

ordered-events-over-integers/1.label: ordered logical events over checked integers
ordered-events-over-integers/1.legend_header: Theory: ordered logical events over checked integers. sigma is the declared trace, i its zero-based active position. A prime reads after this event; it is neither negation nor a derivative. Boolean algebra uses a different prime convention outside this theory. Next advances one recorded event. Empty event traces are refused. Initialization is checked separately. Trace quantifiers can be vacuous over an empty execution domain; machine initialization must establish nonemptiness.

forall: the statement after the colon holds for each {v} in {domain}; true if {domain} is empty
exists: the statement after the colon holds for some {v} in {domain}; false if {domain} is empty
exists1: one and no more member satisfies the statement; false if the domain is empty
=>: when the left side is true the right side must be; when it is false there is no demand
<=>: both sides have the same truth value
not: true exactly when the following statement is false
or: at least one statement must hold; both may hold
*: checked i128 multiplication; overflow is indeterminate
+: checked i128 addition; overflow is indeterminate
-: checked i128 subtraction; overflow is indeterminate
ceil: the least integer at or above u/v; signed checked i128 arithmetic, nonzero divisor; undefined arithmetic is indeterminate
floor: the greatest integer at or below u/v; signed checked i128 arithmetic, nonzero divisor; undefined arithmetic is indeterminate
count: the number of distinct members that satisfy the condition

always: Every remaining event, including now; other traces require the visible trace quantifier.
eventually: A witness now or later; finite and unbounded modes differ.
next: The immediately following recorded event; false at a finite endpoint.
until: Strong until: the right operand must occur, possibly now; the left need not hold at that witness.
within: Offsets 0 through the displayed bound inclusive; events are not seconds.
